findings.description: STG Group, a Petaluma company, bought eight floors of this eleven-storey Mid-Market office building in August 2026 for roughly $8 million according to city records — a fraction of the $80 million the space was valued at in 2015. The seller, LightHouse for the Blind and Visually Impaired, had bought the top three floors for its headquarters and a majority stake in the lower eight; city agencies had occupied the lower floors since 1999, including the Treasurer & Tax Collector and the Environment Department, and moved out when their leases came up in 2024. Both parties are organisations; the individuals quoted in the story are not recorded here.

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses has 1155 MARKET ST but it does not join to one parcel. 1155 MARKET ST's coordinates fall in 4 active parcels (3702821, 3702823, 3702822, 3702820), which is what a condominium looks like in sf-parcels: one parcel per unit, none of them the building.
resolution.note: The address is a condominium today, and the directory contract in the root AGENTS.md defers those: each unit has its own parcel and none of them is the building the record names.

publish.note: The seeder may not make a page here. 1155 Market Street is a commercial condominium: EAS carries it only as #PARCEL A, B, C and D, on four active parcels (3702820-3702823), and the directory contract in the root AGENTS.md defers that case because none of the four parcels is the building. That subdivision is the story — STG bought eight floors and LightHouse kept the top three — so the fact is real and has nowhere legitimate to go today. If the site ever settles how it documents a vertically subdivided building, this is a good first candidate.
